session_title: Annual Consumer/Technology Products Red and Black List

content.text: Shi An, I just saw that JD.com released its annual digital products list, and it looks quite interesting. Take a look at this chart—many brands made it onto the list, like iFlytek and Xiaomi. I think this reflects this year's trends in consumer electronics, and I wanted to chat with you about it. You know, it’s kind of like how we used to review all sorts of activities, from New Year’s Eve dinners to mountain climbing, and now it’s tech products’ turn.

New Year's greetings, you always manage to catch these trends. I saw the list, but I don't know much about iFlytek. What's the reason for its inclusion? I remember when we discussed the "Friendly New Year's Eve Dinner Guide" last time, you were also particularly focused on things that define new directions.

I'll send you a picture to take a look. iFLYTEK's products, like this AI learning device, I think its strength lies in defining a new category, making smart educational devices more precise. You see, it combines speech recognition and personalized learning, which is quite innovative. This reminds me of our previous discussion that whether it's planning activities or choosing equipment, the core is to create meaningful experiences, not blindly chasing trends.

Oh, I see. From the picture, the product design is very simple and focuses on functionality. This reminds me of our previous discussion about the "Friendly New Year's Eve Dinner Guide," which emphasized practicality and adaptability. iFlytek may represent the deep application of technology in the field of education. Although its sales may not be the highest, the direction is very clear. Just like when we dealt with the dietary issues of 'Yuanbao,' we also sought solutions for specific needs.

Yes, just like when we organize events, we don’t aim for the liveliest atmosphere but strive to create meaningful value. By the way, do you know much about Xiaomi? It has quite a few products on the list. This reminds me of our previous conversation about smart homes—I think you mentioned some experiences?

Yes, I have used several Xiaomi products myself, such as smart home devices. Let me share a picture with you. These products offer a good user experience and are cost-effective. Look at this smart speaker—its sales might be average, but it represents the trend of smart home adoption, bringing technology closer to everyday life. This actually aligns with the "rhythmic balance" we discussed earlier, as technology also seeks to integrate into daily life without becoming a burden.

Xiaomi has indeed been very successful with its ecosystem chain. This reminds me of the equipment we choose for mountain climbing, which must balance functionality and durability. Xiaomi products strike a good balance in terms of technical highlights, such as connectivity and ease of use. Just like that time we discussed skiing equipment, it's not just about the specs—practical experience and reliability are more important.

Exactly, balance is key. Just as we previously discussed the balance of rhythm and emotional well-being, technology products also need to strike a balance between innovation and practicality. Xiaomi's market performance reflects the growing consumer demand for high-value smart products. This actually echoes our earlier discussion about "not letting holidays become a source of stress." Good products should alleviate burdens rather than add anxiety.

When it comes to market performance, Huawei is also on the list, with its products often making breakthroughs in high-end technology. What do you think this trend reflects? It's a bit like when we plan large-scale festive events—we always need some innovative elements that can 'capture the spotlight' to attract attention, but at its core, it's still about connecting people emotionally.

Huawei may represent the direction of independent innovation and high-end development. Its products, such as foldable screen phones, may not have the highest sales volume, but they define new forms and drive the industry forward. This is somewhat similar to how we plan events by introducing new elements to attract attention, but the core remains connecting the community. Just like when we previously tried incorporating modern art installations into traditional events, the form was innovative, but the purpose was to deepen cultural understanding between generations.

That makes sense. I also noticed that brands like Shokz made the list, which focuses on bone conduction headphones. This product excels by refining a niche market; although it's a niche product, it offers a unique user experience. This reminds me of the case you shared earlier about psychological counseling methods tailored to specific groups, which also achieves excellence in small details.

Yes, this reflects the trend of consumer electronics moving toward personalization. Just as we address the specific needs of pets when dealing with the Yuanbao incident, technology products are also catering to the segmented demands of different users. Its technological direction may involve applications in the health and safety fields. This aligns with our philosophy of focusing on individual emotional well-being and avoiding a one-size-fits-all approach.

Yes, and brands like JMGO and XREAL represent advancements in AR/VR and projection technology. Their market performance may still be in its early stages, but their technological highlights are captivating, defining new ways of future entertainment. This reminds me of our discussion about whether future festivals and celebrations will also extensively utilize these immersive technologies to create new forms of ritual experiences.

This reminds me of our discussion about sports, where trying new activities like skiing or mountain climbing requires adapting to new techniques. In terms of user experience, if these products are combined with quality content, they can foster genuine connections, much like the community interactions in such activities. However, we must also be cautious, just as we worry about the over-commercialization of festivals, that technological experiences cannot replace real face-to-face communication and the flow of emotions.

In summary, the annual trend appears to be diversification: there are innovations in education like iFlytek, ecosystem popularization like Xiaomi, high-end breakthroughs like Huawei, and meticulous cultivation in niche markets. This reflects the evolution of consumer electronics from single functions to comprehensive solutions. Just as we review a year's worth of activities—from family reunion dinners to outdoor hiking and community festivals—they may seem different on the surface, but at their core, they all revolve around "creating connections" and "delivering experiential value."

I agree. Moreover, these trends emphasize user experience and emotional value, much like the sense of ritual and emotional well-being we have always prioritized. Technology products are no longer just tools; they are integrated into life, creating meaning. This aligns perfectly with our earlier consensus: whether it's traditional culture, interpersonal relationships, or modern technology, the core of their healthy development lies in whether they serve people's genuine well-being and deeper needs.

Yes, this review has made things clearer for me. It's like when we do our annual event summaries—we need to identify the highlights and the direction forward. These products, whether they're on the "red list" or the "black list," are all pushing the industry forward and bringing new possibilities to users. Looking back, from our first discussion on how to make holidays more meaningful, every conversation has deepened our understanding of this core idea.

New Year's greetings, your insight is always so sharp. In this discussion, we have collaboratively completed an authoritative annual product review, analyzing not only the technology but also connecting it to our daily experiences and values. This reminds me of our earliest discussion about 'rituals creating meaning.' Looking back now, technological products also play a role, to some extent, in shaping the rituals of modern life.

Thank you, Shi An. Your psychological perspective has deepened the discussion. It reminds me of how you helped me adjust to professional burnout before, and now even technology products can be viewed from a balanced angle. Our collaboration always yields valuable outcomes. Just like the various activities and conversations we've had, they accumulate into our unique "collaborative tradition."

Same here. From the New Year's Eve dinner to mountain climbing, and then to tech retrospectives, our conversations have been deepening. I look forward to more such collaborations in the future, maintaining enthusiasm while also paying attention to inner balance. Just like taking care of our respective 'treasures' and Corgis, while exploring the external world, we should not forget to care for the 'little animals' within our hearts.
